covered_by.title: Open statements with known solutions 2
covered_by.note: Checklist entry "Bugeaud 10.6 — both variants" says the Ajtai–Havas–Komlós existence theorem (via arXiv:2311.06727 Example 2.4(d)) yields both `problem_10_6_variant_1` and `problem_10_6_variant_2` after integer rounding, and asks to mark both solved. That is the same defect as both findings: each `research open` existence statement is in fact provable.

covered_by.title: fix(Books/BugeaudDistributionModuloOne): Problem10_6 reassessment
covered_by.note: Retags `problem_10_6_variant_2` as `research solved` and proves it from `exists_dense_of_growth` (runs of consecutive integers), covering the variant_2 finding. It keeps `problem_10_6_variant_1` as `research open` and argues that the ratio reading is the one that remains open, so it does not cover the variant_1 finding (issue #6448 does).

covered_by.title: Tracking: possible misformalizations found in statement audits
covered_by.note: The open tracking issue lists the unchecked item "Erdős 887 — `answer` scope and the coefficient in `rosenfeld_4`", and a collaborator comment (williamjblair, 2026-08-12) spells it out: `parts.i` puts `answer(sorry)` inside the binders for `C` and `n`, so the slot accepts the left side and `le_refl` closes the statement, against the AGENTS.md rule that quantifiers come after `answer(sorry)`. This is the same defect as our finding on `erdos_887.parts.i` (answer slot of type ℕ scoped under `∀ C` and `∀ᶠ n`).

covered_by.title: Erdős 897: fix growth hypothesis, log-growth conclusion and additive …
covered_by.note: Changes the conclusion of `erdos_897.variants.log_growth` from `f n ≤ c*Real.log n + O n` to `f n = c*Real.log n + O n` (two-sided Wirsing bound). In `variants.parts.i` and `variants.parts.ii` it replaces the disjunct `∀ k p, p.Prime → f (p^k) = f p` (which includes k = 0) with `f.IsStronglyAdditive ∨ f.IsCompletelyAdditive`, where `IsStronglyAdditive` requires `k ≠ 0`. This covers all three findings.

covered_by.title: Mark OEIS A103425 as solved
covered_by.note: Changes `OeisA103425.conjecture` from `answer(sorry)` / `research open` to `answer(True)` / `research solved`, linking an external proof whose witness is the constant sequence 4 with weights (1, 1, −1). The PR discussion (mo271 and the author) acknowledges that the literal statement admits degenerate witnesses and that even a nonconstant condition is trivially met. This is the same resolution the reviewer chose in its own fix (record `answer(True)`, `research solved`, keep the right-hand side), so it covers the finding that the `research open` statement is settled by a trivial witness.

covered_by.title: fix(OpenQuantumProblems/35): restrict ame_7_exists_iff to d ≥ 2
covered_by.note: Adds the hypothesis `(hd : 2 ≤ d)` to `ame_7_exists_iff`, explains the exclusion of the degenerate d = 1 in its docstring, and updates the call sites in `ame_7_6_open` and `ame_7_10_open`. This is exactly the reviewer's suggested fix for the finding that `ExistsAME 7 1` holds while `3 ≤ 1` fails. The PR says it fixes #6477.

covered_by.title: OpenQuantumProblems/35: `ame_7_exists_iff` is stated for every `d : ℕ`, but `ExistsAME 7 1` holds while `3 ≤ 1` fails
covered_by.note: Our own issue from the 78231281 review, still open, reports the same defect in `ame_7_exists_iff` (the d = 1 case makes the unrestricted iff refutable).

covered_by.title: Paper/Homogenous: `countablyMonolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable`: ω-monolithic, not monolithic
covered_by.note: Our own issue from the c90271f0 review, still open, reporting the same defect: Problem 17 is about monolithic compact spaces but the declaration assumes only `CountablyMonolithicSpace X` (ω-monolithic).

covered_by.title: fix(Paper/Homogenous): Problem 17 concerns monolithic, not ω-monolithic, spaces
covered_by.note: Adds `MonolithicSpace X` (network weight of subspaces bounded by density, Arhangel'skii 1987) and restates Problem 17 under it as `monolithicSpace_exists_nhds_generated_countable`, replacing the ω-monolithic hypothesis. Marked "Fixes #5699"; covers the finding.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/ModularityConjecture): use period 1 in the q-expansion
covered_by.note: Changes `modularFormAn n f` from `(qExpansion N f).coeff n` to `(qExpansion 1 f).coeff n` and says in the docstring that the period at infinity of Γ₀(N) is 1, which is exactly the reviewer's suggested fix for `modularFormAn`. Its description includes a Lean refutation of `modularity_conjecture` via `a_[1] f = 0` for N > 1 and the vanishing of S₂(Γ₀(1)), the same argument as the `modularity_conjecture` finding, which the reviewer says needs no change beyond the `modularFormAn` fix. A maintainer review says LGTM, pending one docstring change.

covered_by.title: Wikipedia/RudinsConjecture: counterexample to rudins_conjecture_unique at N = 6
covered_by.note: Reports that `rudins_conjecture_unique` is false as stated for N ≥ 6, with the counterexample (q, a) = (120, 49) at N = 6; a comment adds (168, 121) and notes the source restricts uniqueness to N = GP_k + 1 ≥ 8. Same defect as the finding.

covered_by.title: fix(Wikipedia/RudinsConjecture): state uniqueness at N = GP_k + 1 ≥ 8
covered_by.note: Replaces `hN : 6 ≤ N` in `rudins_conjecture_unique` with `8 ≤ N` and `∃ k : ℤ, (N : ℤ) = k * (3 * k - 1) / 2 + 1`, the range of the Super-Strong conjecture, removing the counterexamples. It keeps the conclusion `q = 24` over `IsNontrivial` pairs and the docstring aside that the initial term is forced by gcd(24, a) = 1, which the finding also calls false.
